Series::multinomial¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::multinomial() const
Series Series::multinomial(std::int64_t num_samples) const
Series Series::multinomial(std::int64_t num_samples, bool replacement) const

What It Does¶

Treats the last axis of the receiver as a list of category weights and returns sampled category indices — not probabilities, not one-hot vectors, just int64 positions along that axis.

  • A 1-D receiver is one distribution; the result is [num_samples].

  • A 2-D receiver is one distribution per row; rows are sampled independently and stay rows: [rows, categories] → [rows, num_samples].

Weights do not need to sum to 1 — only their ratios matter, so [1, 2, 7] and [0.1, 0.2, 0.7] sample identically. A zero-weight category is never chosen. Negative, NaN, infinite, or all-zero rows are rejected, not repaired.

The overloads:

call

num_samples

replacement

multinomial()

1

true

multinomial(n)

n

false

multinomial(n, r)

n

r

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the indices; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

num_samples (std::int64_t): how many indices to draw per distribution. Must be positive. With replacement = false it cannot exceed the number of categories — nor, in any row, the number of positive-weight categories.

replacement (bool): with true, a category may be drawn repeatedly and num_samples can exceed the category count. With false, each drawn category is removed from that row’s remaining choices.

Returns¶

Series An int64 tensor of category indices. Shape [num_samples] for a 1-D receiver, [rows, num_samples] for a 2-D one.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver rank is not 1 or 2

  • if the receiver dtype is not floating-point

  • if num_samples <= 0

  • if any row has a non-positive sum, or contains a negative / non-finite weight

  • if replacement = false and num_samples exceeds the (positive-weight) category count

Gradient¶

Not differentiable — discrete indices carry no derivative back to the weights.

Examples¶

Example 1. 1-D weights → indices, with replacement. Weights [1, 2, 7] favor category 2. Seeded, so fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto w = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 7.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, w.multinomial(12, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[12], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2]

Category 2 carries 7/10 of the weight, so it dominates a small draw.

Example 2. Over a large sample the empirical frequencies match the normalized weights.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto w = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 7.0});
auto s = w.multinomial(100000, true);
auto v = s.to_vec<long long>();
long c0 = 0, c1 = 0, c2 = 0;
for (auto x : v) { if (x == 0) ++c0; else if (x == 1) ++c1; else ++c2; }
std::cout << "freq: " << c0 / 1e5 << " " << c1 / 1e5 << " " << c2 / 1e5
          << "  (weights normalize to 0.1 0.2 0.7)\n";

Output¶

freq: 0.09959 0.20101 0.6994  (weights normalize to 0.1 0.2 0.7)

Example 3. A 2-D receiver samples each row independently. Here each row has a single possible category, so the result is deterministic.

pluss::rng_seed(1);
auto w = pluss::make_series({{0.0, 1.0, 0.0},
                             {1.0, 0.0, 0.0}});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, w.multinomial(4, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1 1 1 1 ⎤
⎣ 0 0 0 0 ⎦

Row 0 can only pick category 1; row 1 only category 0.

Example 4. replacement = false gives distinct indices — and num_samples cannot exceed the category count.

pluss::rng_seed(2);
auto w = pluss::make_series({1.0, 3.0, 6.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, w.multinomial(3, false));
try {
  auto bad = pluss::make_series({1.0, 3.0, 6.0}).multinomial(5, false);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 2, 1]multinomial: cannot sample more entries than categories without replacement

All three indices are distinct; the weights bias which comes first, and each chosen category’s weight is removed before the next draw.

Example 5. All-zero, negative-weight, and non-floating inputs are all rejected.

try {
  pluss::make_series({0.0, 0.0}).multinomial(1);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  pluss::make_series({1.0, -1.0}).multinomial(1);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3}).multinomial(1);   // int64 weights
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

multinomial: each probability row must have a positive sum
multinomial: probabilities must be finite and nonnegative
multinomial: probabilities must have a floating-point dtype

Example 6. Reproducible under a fixed seed.

pluss::rng_seed(9);
auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}).multinomial(6, true);
pluss::rng_seed(9);
auto b = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}).multinomial(6, true);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "a == b: " << a.equal(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The result is indices, int64, along the last axis — not probabilities, not one-hot rows.

  • Weights are relative. They do not need to sum to 1; a row of all zeros is an error, not “uniform”.

  • replacement = false capacity: num_samples must not exceed the category count, or the number of positive-weight categories in any row.

  • The receiver rank must be exactly 1 or 2, and the dtype must be floating-point.

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

multinomial(num_samples, replacement = false) draws category indices from last-axis weights:

  • 1-D → [num_samples]; 2-D → [rows, num_samples], rows independent

  • weights are relative and must be nonnegative with a positive row sum

  • replacement = false gives distinct indices, capped by the category count

  • int64 result; reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); not differentiable

See Also¶

  • Series::bernoulli: independent binary events (the two-category, one-sample special case is close in spirit).

  • Series::random_: uniform integers over a range — no weighting.

  • pluss::series::multinomial: the free-function form.
